subject: general
question:
In the given figure, A, B, C and D are four points on a circle. AC and BD intersect at point E such that ∠BEC = 130° and ∠ECD = 20°. Find ∠BAC.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fb1d71405cc888552784e65404b7f2bed51c30d3cfaf69564b916e3915ef4d7e.png]
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

By the **Exterior Angle Theorem** in **▵CED**, the exterior angle ∠BEC is equal to the sum of interior opposite angles.

∠BEC = ∠ECD + ∠EDC

⇒ 130° = 20° + ∠EDC

⇒ ∠EDC = 110°

Since **∠BAC** and **∠BDC** (same as ∠EDC) are **angles in the same segment** subtended by **arc BC**, they are equal.

∠BAC = ∠BDC = 110°.

**∴ The correct answer is 110°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** A **circle** with points **A, B, C, D**. Chords **AC** and **BD** intersect at **E**. ∠BEC = 130° and ∠ECD = 20°.

**Formula Used:** Sum of angles on a straight line = 180°; Sum of angles in a triangle = 180°; Angles subtended by the same arc at the circumference are equal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9bd1f9c9f725e39810da860cf3e4cd99796c06b417cf906c224592648fd84012.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ In the figure, **A-E-C** is a straight line.

⇒ ∠BEC + ∠CED = 180° (Linear Pair)

⇒ 130° + ∠CED = 180°

⇒ ∠CED = 180° − 130° = 50°

⇒ Now in **▵CED**, the sum of all interior angles is 180°.

⇒ ∠CED + ∠ECD + ∠EDC = 180°

⇒ 50° + 20° + ∠EDC = 180°

⇒ 70° + ∠EDC = 180°

⇒ ∠EDC = 180° − 70° = 110°

⇒ Note that ∠BDC is the same as ∠EDC, so ∠BDC = 110°.

⇒ **∠BAC** and **∠BDC** are subtended by the same **arc BC** in the same **segment**.

⇒ ∠BAC = ∠BDC = 110°.

**∴ The correct answer is 110°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angles in the Same Segment

Angles subtended by the same arc at any point on the remaining part of the circle are always equal.

Exterior Angle Property of a Triangle

The measure of an exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the measures of its two interior opposite angles.

Cyclic Quadrilateral

A quadrilateral whose all four vertices lie on a circle is called a cyclic quadrilateral, and the sum of its opposite angles is 180°.</p
